en: Jose Rizal wrote the novels Noli Me Tangere and El Filibusterismo to expose Spanish colonial abuses in the Philippines.
The sampaguita, a fragrant white jasmine flower, was declared the national flower of the Philippines in 1934.
The Supreme Court of the Philippines, located in Manila, holds the judicial power to interpret the Constitution.
The Igorot people of the Cordillera mountains built the famous Banaue Rice Terraces over two thousand years ago.
Dr. Fe del Mundo invented a bamboo incubator to provide affordable medical care for infants in rural Philippines.
The carabao, a domesticated swamp buffalo, is the national animal of the Philippines because it helps farmers plow fields.
General Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence from Spain on June 12, 1898, in Kawit, Cavite.
Filipino and English are the two official languages of the Philippine government, alongside over a hundred regional languages.
The Sinulog Festival in Cebu City honors the Santo Niño with a traditional two-steps-forward, one-step-back dance.
The Philippine Constitution guarantees every child the right to basic education, which is free in public schools.
National Artist Fernando Amorsolo is famous for his paintings depicting rural Philippine landscapes bathed in golden sunlight.
Bayanihan is a traditional Filipino value where community members work together to help a family move their house.
